issues.title: New queue-drain wait in stream_close() is never exercised by any test
issues.verdictReason: Verified by building the repo and reverting rpc.cc:562-570 (the queue_drained wait) back to the pre-PR direct write_buf.close(): test_stream_send_after_stream_close still passed 5/5 runs, because sink_impl::close() (rpc_impl.hh:920-924) already awaits the eof-marker send() before calling close_sink(), so _outgoing_queue_ready is already resolved by the time stream_close() runs in this test's scenario.
issues.scopeReason: The untested code is new in this PR (commit f545c28a).

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: New wait-for-queue step in stream_close() is never exercised by a test

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/ironweave/revie: The sink's close awaits its end-of-stream send() before close_sink(), so the queue is already empty when stream_close() runs in the test; removing or breaking lines 562-570 fails no test.

issues.title: Doc says connection shuts down "only once both halves are closed", which is false
issues.verdictReason: Confirmed other shutdown paths bypass the both-halves-closed invariant: client::abort_all_streams() (rpc.cc:847) aborts a stream unconditionally, connection::handle_stream_frame() sets _error=true directly on a bad read (rpc.cc:585-588) without going through stream_close(), and stop_send_loop() tears the connection down on any fatal error. The doc's own line 49-50 acknowledges aborting is distinct from closing, but line 115 still states the shutdown-only-via-both-halves claim as an unqualified absolute.
issues.scopeReason: This doc section is new in this PR (commit 69da8f5b).

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Doc claim "shut down only once both halves are closed" is false

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/ironweave/revie: The connection is also shut down by closing the parent client (abort_all_streams, rpc.cc:848), by the peer reaching EOF (rpc.cc:588), and by the loop-exit stop_send_loop (rpc.cc:1062); the same doc contradicts itself at line 49.

issues.title: Doc says reading-until-throws closes the source, false for deserialization errors
issues.verdictReason: Checked source_impl::operator() (rpc_impl.hh:941-982): process_one_buffer() calls unmarshall() directly at lines 945-948 and 980, outside the stream_receive() continuation (961-975) that is the only place close_source() is invoked. An unmarshall exception (e.g. a deserialization error) propagates straight out of operator() without ever calling close_source(), so stream_close() is never triggered, contradicting the doc's claim that throwing closes the source.
issues.scopeReason: This doc section is new in this PR; the mismatched claim was introduced by this PR's own documentation.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Doc claim "reading until it throws closes the source" is false for deserialization errors

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/ironweave/revie: When unmarshall throws inside process_one_buffer (rpc_impl.hh:941/951), close_source() is skipped, so stream_close() never runs, contradicting the documented behavior.

issues.title: Regression test swallows closed_error instead of asserting it was thrown
issues.verdictReason: The try/catch at rpc_test.cc:2016-2020 accepts both a thrown closed_error and a successful (non-throwing) return with no assertion either way; BOOST_REQUIRE_THROW would make the intent explicit. Confirmed empirically though that the test still reliably detects the real regression (reverting the _stream_closing guard made the test fail 4/5 runs on the put_after_close assertion), so the gap is about assertion precision, not detection power.
issues.scopeReason: The test is new in this PR (commit 5e25ebdb).

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Test never asserts the hook actually fails with closed_error

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/ironweave/revie: The try/catch also accepts a successful return, and detection depends on the flush poller having run (10x yield() does not force a poll) or on a process abort at teardown; should use BOOST_REQUIRE_THROW(..., rpc::closed_error).

issues.title: Test doesn't assert error() was still false when the hook fired
issues.verdictReason: Reverting just the _stream_closing guard (restoring `if (!_error)`) made the test fail reliably (4/5 runs on the put_after_close assertion, 1/5 on an earlier unrelated exception), which argues the window is hit correctly rather than being masked by a pre-existing _error=true. But connection::error() is private and unobservable from the test, so there is no direct way to confirm _error was false at the exact moment of the hook call; the claim about test fragility under reordering cannot be fully settled without instrumenting private connection state.
issues.scopeReason: The test is new in this PR (commit 5e25ebdb).

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Test can pass on base code under one ordering, masking the fix's necessity

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/ironweave/revie: If the peer's FIN has already made the client loop set _error, the old !_error guard also refuses the frame; the test never checks that error() was still false when the hook fired.

issues.title: Pre-sink.close() assertion failure would abort the test binary, not fail cleanly
issues.verdictReason: Confirmed ~sink_impl() (rpc_impl.hh:932-936) unconditionally asserts sink_closed() via SEASTAR_ASSERT; if any REQUIRE or unexpected exception fires between the start of the test body and sink.close() (line 2010), stack unwinding destroys `sink` unclosed and aborts the process instead of failing the Boost test cleanly. This is an inherent property of the sink_impl API shared by other stream tests, but this specific test's structure is new and carries the same risk.
issues.scopeReason: The test is new in this PR; its fragility window is part of the new code even though the underlying assertion contract is pre-existing.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Early test failure aborts the whole test binary instead of failing cleanly

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/ironweave/revie: If a REQUIRE fails or an unexpected exception is thrown before sink.close(), the stack unwinds with the sink unclosed and release_close never set, and the SEASTAR_ASSERT in ~sink_impl (rpc_impl.hh:935) then aborts the binary instead of failing the test cleanly.

issues.title: const_cast on this inside const negotiate() to mutate factory state
issues.verdictReason: Confirmed: hook_capturing_compressor_factory::negotiate() is const but const_casts away constness to push_back into its own `hooks` member (line 1957). This is legal (the underlying objects server_factory/client_factory are not actually const), but it diverges from the existing pattern in the same file (tracker::factory at line 1801-1802 holds its mutable state behind a reference member instead, needing no cast) and would be UB if the factory were ever stored/passed as truly const.
issues.scopeReason: New test helper code added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: const_cast on this inside the const negotiate() method

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/ironweave/revie: The factory at line 1801 in the same file keeps its mutable state behind a reference instead; the cast is undefined behaviour if the factory is ever declared const.

issues.title: Comment claims queue_drained can be exceptional, but no code path makes it so
issues.verdictReason: Traced every site that resolves an outgoing_entry::done with an exception (rpc.cc:217, 288, both reached only via withdraw()/stop_send_loop(), both gated on _error already being true as stop_send_loop's first statement) versus connection::send()'s own completion path (always p->done.set_value(), even after abort() on failure, line 338). Since stream_close() only reaches this code under `!error()` and captures queue_drained synchronously with no intervening yield, queue_drained cannot actually be in an exceptional state here; the comment copies reasoning that is valid for the analogous code in stop_send_loop() (rpc.cc:224-226) but does not apply at this call site. The code is still correct since ignore_ready_future() handles both outcomes harmlessly.
issues.scopeReason: The comment is new in this PR.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/ironweave/revie: A comment was claimed to misstate when _outgoing_queue_ready fails, but Codex judged this a false positive.

issues.title: Commits lack DCO Signed-off-by trailer claimed to be required
issues.verdictReason: doc/contributing.md's DCO requirement is explicitly scoped to the git-send-email/mailing-list patch workflow it describes. The repo's top-level CONTRIBUTING.md (the file GitHub actually surfaces for PRs) separately lists "open a GitHub pull request" as an alternative with no DCO mention, and there is no DCO bot or CI check in .github/workflows. The requirement does not apply to this PR's submission route.
issues.scopeReason: doc/contributing.md and CONTRIBUTING.md are untouched by this PR; the question of whether GitHub PRs need DCO sign-off is pre-existing and unrelated to this change's content.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Commits lack the DCO Signed-off-by trailer required by contributing docs

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/ironweave/revie: None of the three commits has a DCO Signed-off-by, which doc/contributing.md:6-10 requires; Codex could not decide whether that rule applies to the GitHub PR route.
